D012-D016_h001.question:
I’ve been feeling on edge more than usual, especially at work. I deal with all kinds of scenes—blood, trauma, you name it—but lately, even going into a routine job has me tense before I even step inside. About six months ago, I started noticing this thing with spiders. Not like, just a startle. It’s… my chest locks up instantly when I see one. Once, I was cleaning an apartment, and a tiny spider dropped from the ceiling into my gear bag. I froze. My heart just took off, I couldn’t breathe right, and I had to leave everything there for the day. I know it sounds extreme, but it's like my body reacts before my brain can catch up.

I’ve tried to work through it, but now I find myself checking corners, bags, even my car tires obsessively—not because I think something bad will happen, but just in case. I don’t like feeling this way—I’ve handled far worse in my line of work. But this isn’t about gore or death. It’s just… spiders. I can’t explain why it hit me so hard, or why it won’t let go. I avoid basements now, even when I shouldn’t. But is it fear? Or am I just checking too much? I don’t know where one ends and the other begins.
D012-D016_h001.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia
D012-D016_h001.answer: B & A. Specific Phobia & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D012-D016_h002.question:
I’ve been feeling this knot in my chest whenever I’m outside and the sky starts to change—like when the clouds roll in, or it gets dark too fast. It’s not that I think something bad will happen, exactly, but my body just… locks up. Last week, I was walking to my car after work during a storm—just rain and wind, nothing extreme—and I remember stopping in the parking lot, unable to take another step. My legs felt like they were glued to the ground. I had to lean against a lamppost until someone from the store came out and asked if I was okay.  

It’s not like I avoid going outside altogether. I go, I work my shifts, I do what I need to. But there’s this moment—a split second when the light changes or thunder cracks—where I can’t move, can’t speak. It passes, usually in a minute or two, but it’s embarrassing. I’m a manager, people look to me, and there I am, frozen like a child.  

I don’t check things over and over or have any rituals. And I don’t actively dread storms—I’ll watch weather reports just fine. It’s only when I’m actually *in* it. But I can’t say I go out of my way to avoid clouds or dark skies, either. It just… happens.
D012-D016_h002.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia
D012-D016_h002.answer: B & A. Specific Phobia & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D012-D016_h003.question:

D012-D016_h003.options:

    B. Specific Phobia

D012-D016_h004.question:

When the sky darkens early, even if there’s no storm coming, I start feeling on edge. I find myself checking the weather constantly, sometimes every hour, just to make sure nothing’s coming. It’s not like I think something terrible will happen if I go outside or anything. I don’t have to do certain things to feel safe. I just… don’t want to risk feeling that way. It’s been like this off and on for about a year now—sometimes better, sometimes worse.

    B. Specific Phobia

    D. Schizophrenia

D012-D016_h005.question:

I don’t avoid storms exactly… I can’t. But I don’t feel in control. It’s like something inside just kicks in, and I can’t shut it off. I don’t know if it’s the fear of the storm itself or… something else it triggers. It’s been like this for months now—not every day, but often enough.

A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D012-D016_h006.question: I’ve been feeling really overwhelmed anytime I have to be in certain places—like tunnels, elevators, or even long highway bridges. I don’t think about it much when I’m at home, but the anticipation before I have to face one of these situations makes me dread the day. I’m not sure if it’s anxiety building up around the place itself, or if there’s something else feeding into it—maybe just how helpless I feel once I’m inside.

    B. Specific Phobia

D012-D016_h007.question: I’ve been having these reactions for a few years now—hard to pin down exactly when they started, but they’ve gotten worse lately. Avoiding stuff isn’t really an option, not as a single dad. I don’t know if it’s fear or something else—I can’t explain why it hits so hard, or why I can’t just shake it off. I’m not doing any rituals or anything like that. I just endure it… same way I did at the hospital.

    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D012-D016_h008.question:

I just can’t bring myself to go. I tell myself I should, but the thought brings on the cold sweat, the tunnel vision. So I stay put. Safe. But it’s shrinking my world, slowly.

A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D012-D016_h009.question:

D012-D016_h011.question:

    B. Specific Phobia

D012-D016_h012.question:
